title: streaming: robust reconnect/resume and server timeout handling with OpenAI compatibility
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improves streaming lifecycle robustness: better client cancel handling, graceful disconnects with resume support, and server-side timeout backoffs. OpenAI compatibility layer updated to match reconnection/resume semantics.
commits: a1f4d8e: design: add reconnect/resume state machine and protocol extensions
c3b9f7a: runtime: implement server-side reconnect token validation and session resumption
d4e2c1b: api: expose resume_id on streaming responses for OpenAI compatibility
f7b3a2c: infra: add integration tests for simulated disconnects and server timeouts
e5a9d0f: docs: streaming lifecycle behavior and migration notes
description:
Background: We see production incidents where transient network disconnects or client-side cancellations leave partially-consumed streaming sessions in limbo, causing wasted GPU work and user-visible failures. The OpenAI compatibility layer currently closes streams on disconnect without a clear resume token, which breaks some client SDKs that expect resume semantics.

What this PR does: Implements a session-level reconnect/resume state machine across the streaming runtime and the OpenAI compatibility layer; exposes a stable resume_id in streaming responses; adds server-side conservative timeout/backoff policies that gracefully transition sessions to a terminal state after configurable inactivity windows; improves client cancel handling so a client-initiated cancel marks the session as cancellable but allows short grace windows for reconnect; and adds tests and docs.

Design highlights:
- Session manager: persistent ephemeral session objects (in-memory + optional short-lived cache) that maintain resume token, last-activity timestamp, and in-flight KV offsets.
- Resume protocol: responses include resume_id and last_event_offset. Clients can reconnect with resume_id to request resumption; server validates token and rehydrates in-flight state where possible.
- Timeout/backoff: server maintains two timeouts: idle_grace (short) and terminal_timeout (long). On idle_grace, server signals to runtime to release batching resources but keeps session metadata for resume; on terminal_timeout, session is torn down. Timeouts are configurable per deployment class (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Client cancel behavior: explicit client cancel (HTTP/WS cancel frame) marks session as client_canceled and triggers an expedited idle_grace. This preserves resume window for a short period to allow quick reconnects (e.g., mobile flaps) but prevents indefinite resource retention.
- OpenAI compatibility: backwards-compatible additions: resume_id is optional for clients that do not rely on resume. When running in openai-compat mode, we emit resume metadata and accept resume requests under the same endpoint semantics as upstream expectations.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests simulate network flaps, server timeouts, and mixed workloads. We added chaos tests that exercise reconnect/resume under high QPS. Rollout plan: feature-flag behind streaming_reconnect; staged rollout to dedicated then hosted with a one-week monitoring window and alert thresholds for increase in resumed sessions or resource churn.

Why now: Recent incidents (see linked Linear ENG-2345) showed user-visible failures and cost spikes. This change reduces wasted GPU work and improves client experience for flaky networks and mobile clients.
review_conversation:
Rohan: Can you clarify how resume tokens are protected and rotated?
Ava: Resume tokens are HMAC-signed with a server key and include an expiry; rotation handled by key versioning. Added tests in openai_compat_test.go.
Yuki: We need to make sure large KV caches aren't rehydrated synchronously on resume (risk of tail latency).
Ava: Agree — we implemented lazy KV rehydration and a circuit that limits synchronous rehydration bytes; details in session_manager.go comments. Added perf unit test.
Ivy: Can this increase memory churn under high reconnect rates?
Ava: We added an adaptive eviction policy tied to autoscaler signals; described in docs and covered by integration_sim.py.
Rohan: CI flakes on integration_sim — please re-run.
Ava: Re-ran CI after fixing a race in session_state_test.go. All checks passed.
Yuki: Approve after nit about logging level for resume failures.
